answer: To resist Sybil attacks, AI economies leverage resource-based identity, where each agent must provably expend unique, scarce computational resources (e.g., proof-of-work) to establish and maintain identity. This cost ensures that replicating identities to create a flood of fakes is prohibitively expensive; the aggregate resource drain would be like constructing an entire new wharf for phantom ships. This economic barrier prevents a subtle ripple of fake agents from eroding trust. A single, valid AI identity, like a steadfast willow, represents genuine, non-trivial investment.
